clue.text: Technology company appearing before United States Congress

parts.note: IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A tech firm's bosses are summoned to testify before the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Technology company' reads as one firm, but splits into two abbreviations taken in reverse order. 'Congress' is not the legislature but sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress in its older sense means sexual intercourse, which is the Latin-derived formal term used here.

clue.text: See 33
Idiot claiming university charged something for teaching

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the word for idiot surrounds the university letter

parts.note: a tit is British slang for a fool
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A fool at a university demanded payment for giving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like billing someone, but 'charged something' is an electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is instruction given to a student, so it is a synonym for teaching.

clue.text: Director tips off member of production team

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or awry, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director passes on a hint to one of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips off' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on DIRECTOR TIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: One who revises and polishes scripts for a film or broadcast works within the production staff.

clue.text: Hazardous energy company's first to be limited by guarantee

indicators.note: being limited by something means being enclosed by it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: first here picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An energy firm's leader faces restrictions under a guarantee scheme that sounds risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company's first' gives C, which joins E inside INSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unsafe or unstable, which makes it a risk, close to hazardous.

clue.text: Reluctance to move home upset irate neighbours

indicators.note: neighbours means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A householder won't move because the angry people next door are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the angry word into ERTIA; 'neighbours' just places the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body or person to stay at rest, a resistance to motion.

clue.text: Get guards returning last month to part company

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to get something is to understand or see it

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: DEC, December, is the final month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone told to collect guards coming back last month before splitting from their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives CED; 'Get' is see in the sense of understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or federation, i.e. to split away from it.

clue.text: Fiddle plays stripped-down rock ballad

indicators.note: to fiddle is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
stripped down means its outer letters are taken off, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A violinist performs a pared-back version of a rock song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped-down' takes ROCK down to OC; with PLAYS, 'Fiddle' rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean song form, often a narrative ballad with topical lyrics.

clue.text: Tell anecdote about stealing car protected by computer key

indicators.note: stealing here means taking in, so the first piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: protected by means enclosed by the following piece

parts.note: ESC is the Escape key on a keyboard
the Mini is a classic British car

explanation.surface: Someone tells a story about a car theft and a computer security key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' makes EMINISC first, and 'stealing' then has 'about' take it in; 'Tell anecdote' is the definition, not part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall and talk about past experiences, much like telling old stories.

clue.text: Lord endlessly describes archaeological project about ancestry

indicators.note: describes in its geometric sense of drawing around, so the trimmed word goes around the rest
endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord
a dig is an archaeological excavation
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An aristocrat goes on at length about a dig into his family's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves PEE, and 'describes' is used in the geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of descent, so it means lineage or family origins.

clue.text: File newspaper article

definitions.meaning: a file is a line of people or things, one behind another, as in soldiers marching
a regular piece by a particular writer in a paper

explanation.surface: Instruction to submit a news piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a line of marching troops and a regular newspaper feature share this one word.

clue.text: Certain pundit used to get confused

indicators.note: being confused means jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confident commentator who once was sure of things now gets muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute is settled and sure, so it is certain.

clue.text: Long queue's left to make way for parking

indicators.note: making way for means stepping aside for a replacement

parts.note: a line is a queue, and the 's stands for is
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A long queue at a car park is moved aside to free up spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb, to yearn, not an adjective describing the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn or ache for something absent, which is to long for it.

clue.text: Tell like-minded fools to recite mind-numbing mantra

parts.note: to tell is an old word for to count, as in a bank teller or telling beads
sheep are people who blindly follow the crowd

explanation.surface: Telling a group of conformist idiots to chant a dull slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' sounds like an instruction to speak, but in its old sense it means to number.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbering imaginary animals jumping a fence is the traditional dull repetition used to fall asleep.

clue.text: He agrees to wedding being re-arranged, leaving one date unavailable

indicators.note: rearranged signals the letters of these words are reordered
leaving means one letter is left out of the jumble

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A man consents to a wedding that's been rescheduled, leaving one day free.
explanation.walkthrough: The seventeen letters of HE AGREES TO WEDDING less one D are rearranged into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person said to be busy with something else cannot be reached, so they are unavailable.

clue.text: One acknowledges waiting lorry

definitions.meaning: someone who rewards service at table with extra money
a dump truck whose body tilts to unload

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a lorry is held up in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who gives gratuities to waiters and a tipping lorry.

clue.text: Romeo's first and last lines some mimic

indicators.note: lines as a verb means fills the inside of, so the letters go within

parts.note: part means some of something

indicators.note: first and last means the opening and closing letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: An actor playing Romeo learns only his first and last lines, some of which he copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' takes the R and O of Romeo; 'lines' is a verb meaning fills, not speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot repeats words without understanding, so as a verb it means to copy or imitate.

clue.text: See 15
Quite a bit sooner

explanation.surface: Quite a lot earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means fairly or considerably, and also preferably, as in I would prefer.

clue.text: Holding practice game breaches code of conduct

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the breaches word goes around the rest

parts.note: holes are breaches or gaps in a wall
use means custom or practice
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Keeping up practice games breaks the rules of behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like part of the description of the game, but it is the containment signal working on 'breaches'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rules laid down by a particular establishment form its code of conduct.

clue.text: See 17
Imagine writer had worried endlessly

parts.note: I'D is the writer of the clue saying I had

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: eaten in the sense of eaten up with worry, i.e. anxious

explanation.surface: An author pictures having fretted without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is crossword shorthand for I, the setter, so 'writer had' gives I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas or concepts in the mind, which means to imagine.

clue.text: See 19
See 13
See 14
See 16
Casual worker depressed by not working

indicators.note: in a down clue, being pressed down by means coming beneath the other piece

parts.note: off means switched off or not working
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm

explanation.surface: A temporary employee is feeling low about being unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'depressed by' puts HAND below OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unceremonious, showing little attention or care.

clue.text: See 18
Strange ladies perhaps stuffing headless rabbit

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so the piece goes inside
headless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: bunny is a child's word for a rabbit
can is slang for a toilet, of which the ladies is one example

explanation.surface: Odd women stuffing a rabbit with no head, a bizarre kitchen scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' is a British word for a women's toilet, hence the slang CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means eerie or weird in a way that is hard to explain.

clue.text: See 4
Broadcast about doubtful case for asylum

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around

parts.note: to beam is to transmit a signal

indicators.note: case means the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A programme airs on a questionable case for granting asylum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes only the outside letters of 'doubtful'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethlem Royal Hospital in London was a notorious lunatic asylum known by this name.

clue.text: Show off little black dress that's seen better days?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black
a rag is a worn, tatty garment

explanation.surface: Flaunting a little black dress that is past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little black dress' wants to be read as one phrase; it splits after 'black'.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is a way of showing off.

clue.text: Criminal cut lead off Paddington's cladding

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook hacks the leading off Paddington's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington Bear, the British children's character, wears a blue toggled coat; 'Paddington' could also be the London station, whose roof might be leaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear's signature garment is a hooded toggle coat of thick woollen cloth.

clue.text: Speech for audience is vital thing to have on record

definitions.meaning: a remark an actor makes to the audience, unheard by others on stage

definitions.text: vital thing to have on record
definitions.meaning: the main side of a single, carrying the lead track

explanation.surface: A speech intended for listeners must be on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage remark addressed to the audience shares spelling with the A-side of a record.

clue.text: This leads to experience identical to draught Guinness when pouring

definitions.text: This leads to experience identical to draught Guinness when pouring

parts.words: This leads to experience identical to draught Guinness when pouring
parts.note: describes the nitrogen-filled device in a can of stout that makes it foam like a pub pint

explanation.surface: A boast that canned stout pours exactly like the draught pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gadget in a can releases gas when opened, creating the creamy head of pub stout.

clue.text: Can late action transform what contributes to sea level?

indicators.note: to transform is to change the form of, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Can late action change the factors that raise sea levels?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a great body of seawater helps make up the level of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast body of water is part of the world's seas, so it contributes to their level.

clue.text: Depicted red deer roaming around the East End of London

indicators.note: around means placed about the other piece
roaming means wandering, so the letters are rearranged
the east end of a word is its last letter, as east is on the right of a map

explanation.surface: Deer wandering around London's East End are shown in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is London's traditionally working-class district, but here it means the final letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a subject is to represent it in art, so rendered means depicted.

clue.text: Chaos could produce new border

parts.note: may expresses possibility, as could does
to hem is to sew an edge onto fabric

explanation.surface: Disorder might result in a new frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and confusion, the same idea as chaos.
